newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold again with crude, bunkers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold again with crude, bunkers.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices, stayed little changed again Tuesday, still supported by a firm bunker market and relatively high crude prices, industry sources said.

"Bunkers are still supporting high sulphurs, and as long as crude holds, I think we can see plus signs on resid," said one cash trader, adding utility demand was lacking but there was little prompt oil available.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent again held steady at about $21.25 a barrel, with Nov paper off slightly with NYMEX to $21.25-40 and Dec also modestly lower at $21.40-60.
NYH Jan one percent paper was quoted at $21.70-90.
High sulphur grades in New York also were unchanged, with 2.2 percent firmly supported by bunkers near the $20 mark.
A trader said 125,000 barrels of prompt 2.8 percent material (250 vis) may have sold at $20.50 (delivered Philadelphia) but the deal could not be confirmed.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices remained stable, with one percent still at $20.00-25 and three percent at about $20.50.
Gas at the New York City gate was unchanged Tuesday in the mid-$2.60s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
